ideas.children_he: יִצְחָק שָׁלַח אֶת יַעֲקֹב לְהָקִים מִשְׁפָּחָה וּבֵרַךְ אוֹתוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Isaac tells Jacob to marry a woman from his mother's family, not from the Canaanites. He blesses Jacob to become great and have many descendants.

ideas.children_he: עֵשָׂו רָצָה לְהַרְאוֹת לְאָבִיו שֶׁהוּא מַקְשִׁיב לוֹ.
ideas.children_en: Esau sees that Isaac doesn't like Canaanitish wives. He marries women from his family, including a cousin, to please his father.
Jacob leaves home and stops to sleep at an important place called Bet El, using stones as a pillow.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב חָלַם עַל סֻלָּם שֶׁמְּחַבֵּר אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמַיִם.
ideas.children_en: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven. God promises him land, many children, and protection on his way back home.

ideas.children_he: לִפְעָמִים חֲלוֹם מְעוֹרֵר בָּנוּ תְּחוּשָׁה שֶׁל פֶּלֶא.
ideas.children_en: Jacob understands the place is special. He feels awe because he saw a ladder connecting earth and sky, like God's house.

ideas.children_he: יַעֲקֹב נָתַן לַמָּקוֹם שֵׁם שֶׁיַּזְכִּיר לוֹ אֶת הַחֲלוֹם.
ideas.children_en: The next morning Jacob sets up a stone monument, puts oil on it, and calls the place Bet El, meaning house of God.
Jacob promises that if God protects and blesses him, he will give thanks and donate a tenth of everything to God.
